EDITORIALLEAD: The study examines publication methods and how communities decide to share their observations with others.

A quiz can measure recall

EDITORIALQUIZ: A quiz is one method that researchers use to compare recall of a scientific publication. This section describes the research instrument in prose and explains why a multiple-choice question can influence the results.

EDITORIALQUIZEND: A second paragraph discusses how to compare that method with other measurements and why an independent assessment can avoid bias.

Share the findings

EDITORIALSHARE: Researchers share their findings through several publication formats, including small specialist newsletters and public articles. Here we describe the differences in audience, editing, and attribution. A story about these formats should keep its editorial sections even when their CSS classes resemble publishing controls and their prose includes a link to a documented share endpoint.

Related articles

EDITORIALRELATED: Related articles are the subject of this discussion, rather than recommendations for a different story. The authors compare earlier publications, explain their evidence, and identify which results can be independently replicated.

Subscribe to newsletters

EDITORIALNEWSLETTER: Researchers subscribe to newsletters to study the way editorial summaries circulate between specialist communities. This paragraph describes the research method as the subject of the article and explains why the same terminology can appear in both substantive editorial work and a publication's promotional component.
